ranges: SPDX/module purpose and imports: HashMap, Range, Arc, core Error/Result/DeepSizeOf, prost Message, custom serde traits, Fragment/generated protobuf, U64Segment, RowIdSequence and read_row_ids. Dataset update version is not a file-format version or stable row ID. The module is public through rowids::version (rust/lance-table/src/rowids.rs:17-24).

LoadedRowLineage is public Debug/Clone/Default with optional Arc row_ids, created_at and last_updated_at sequences. SpilledRowLineage aliases HashMap<u64,LoadedRowLineage> keyed by fragment ID. The contract says an IO-capable caller preloads spilled sequences because synchronous manifest construction has no store; inline sequences need not be included. Defaults are all None/empty map; no loader, validation, timestamp or IO is implemented by these declarations.

RowDatasetVersionRun derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/DeepSizeOf with public span:U64Segment and version:u64. Docs define span over positional offsets rather than stable IDs, enabling alignment with RowIdSequence order. len()->usize and is_empty delegate to span; version copies the scalar. Direct construction permits arbitrary segment shape/values, including empty runs; no invariant validator here.

RowDatasetVersionSequence derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/DeepSizeOf/Default around public Vec<RowDatasetVersionRun>. RowDatasetVersionCursor is pub(crate), Debug/Default, with private run index, intra-run offset, absolute position, optional cached run length, optional Vec run starts and indexed total; tests add seek counter. Cursor does not borrow, identify or hash its source sequence, so reuse assumes the same unchanged sequence.

Private seek_indexed lazily builds one start offset per run and total length by ordinary usize additions. This allocates O(number of runs) memory once; it does not rebuild when another/mutated sequence is supplied. Empty runs produce duplicate starts. Construction calls general run.len, and overflow/malformed segment arithmetic is not checked here.

Indexed seek rejects position>=cached total with Internal text containing position and total. Otherwise unwrap cached starts, binary-search position or take preceding start, then advance across every following start<=position to skip duplicate starts/empty runs. Sets run index, relative offset and position, clears cached length, increments test counter. Bounds failure may leave a newly built index installed but does not set a new position.

current_run repeatedly gets the current run, caching its length. Range fast path uses (end-start) as usize; all other spans delegate len. If offset>=length, advance run and reset offset/cache until a usable run or None. It skips any number of empty runs and never consults absolute span positions for ordering. Range subtraction/cast and index increments are ordinary arithmetic; malformed reverse ranges are not rejected here.

extend_range appends to caller Vec. Empty or reversed Range<usize> returns Ok immediately without validating bounds or moving cursor. A backwards start triggers indexed seek; after an index exists, every non-adjacent start in either direction uses it. Before indexing, forward gaps advance run lengths in place without output, returning Internal if exhausted. Existing cursor/output is not reset or cleared.

For each selected portion, current_run yields version/length and repeat_n appends count=min(request remainder,run remainder), then advances position/offset. Exhaustion returns Internal at current consumed position; output and cursor may already contain partial progress. No reserve, cancellation or async boundary. Adjacent traversal costs visited runs plus emitted values; repeated unindexed forward scanning is monotonic, indexed jumps add binary-search work.

new returns no runs. from_uniform_row_count(row_count:u64,version) returns empty for zero, otherwise exactly one Range(0..row_count) run. It neither checks fragment maximum count/usize fit nor rejects any version, and allocates only the run vector rather than per-row versions.

from_versions scans adjacent u64 values, emits a Range for each change and one final run if nonempty. Spans use global slice positions starting0, versions are exact values; empty input gives empty, uniform input one run. O(input rows) scan and up to O(rows) runs; usize indices/length cast to u64 without checked conversion. It merges adjacent equal values only, not equal values separated by others.

len sums run.len() cast to u64 with ordinary addition. is_empty is true for no runs or all-empty runs. versions constructs a borrowing VersionsIter; cursor returns a default unbound cursor and does not inspect self. Public runs remain mutable and no cached index lives in the sequence itself.

version_at linearly accumulates usize run lengths and returns the first run whose cumulative end exceeds index, else None. It ignores span numeric values and gaps, using concatenated positional lengths; zero-length runs contribute nothing. Cost O(visited runs), ordinary offset+length arithmetic, no random-access index in this method.

get_version_for_row_id scans RowIdSequence segments in stored order, first checks segment bounding range contains the ID and then position(row_id). On first match it calls version_at(prefix lengths+local position), otherwise adds segment length and continues. It does not assert equal row-ID/version lengths or unique IDs. Segment range supplies stored bounds and position then checks actual presence (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:360-431); no whole-dataset lookup or IO occurs.

rows_with_version_greater_than zips row_ids.iter with lazy versions, filters strictly greater than threshold and collects owned Vec IDs. Zip silently stops at the shorter iterator, with no alignment error. It preserves row-ID iteration order and includes no deletion filtering beyond what supplied sequences already encode. VersionsIter empty-run caveat applies.

mask consumes u32 positions once, tracks cumulative original run lengths before mutating each run and passes relative positions to span.mask. It implicitly needs ascending valid positions, but does not sort, deduplicate or validate them; a later position below the current run start can underflow subtraction. Remaining positions at/above final cutoff are ignored. Removes empty spans afterward, does not merge equal-version neighbors or rebase surviving span values, and always returns Ok locally. Segment mask is now covered: list cardinality equal to segment length clears all regardless of entries, and other paths assume ordered unique in-bounds positions (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:694-746).

Public VersionsIter borrows runs and stores private run index, remaining count and current value. new initializes zeros then advance_run loads only the current run, or leaves remaining0 at exhaustion. It does not skip empty runs in advance_run. No allocation, size_hint override or ExactSize/DoubleEnded/FusedIterator implementation appears.

Iterator::next advances by at most one run when remaining count is0, returning None if beyond the list; otherwise it loads that run, saturating-decrements count and returns the version even if the loaded run is empty. Thus [length1/version7,length0/version9] expands to [7,9], a source-derived counterexample not executed here. Consecutive empty runs can likewise emit phantom values. This differs from cursor/version_at, which skip empty spans.

RowDatasetVersionMeta derives Debug/Clone/equality/DeepSizeOf: Inline(Arc<[u8]>) shares encoded bytes; Column is an empty marker locating reserved creation/update hidden fields via Fragment::row_lineage_file. Column requires IO through a dataset loader; this type stores no path or count. Private serde ColumnMarker has no fields, defining the empty-object column arm.

Serialize creates an untagged local Helper: Inline {inline:&[u8]} or Column {column:ColumnMarker}. JSON inline is a numeric byte sequence under inline; column is {column:{}}. Bytes are borrowed for serialization, not decoded. Serializer failures propagate; local helper variants exist only within serialize.

Deserialize uses untagged local Helper with Vec<u8> or empty marker, then allocates Arc::from(inline) or returns Column. It does not decode/validate version bytes, intern equivalent payloads or require a dataset context. No deny_unknown_fields annotation is present; exact unknown-field/ambiguous-arm acceptance delegates serde.

from_sequence writes protobuf bytes and wraps Arc, returning Ok with no explicit Result error branch. load_sequence decodes Inline; Column returns NotSupported explaining fragment metadata alone cannot decode a data-file column. These synchronous methods perform no IO and no physical-row count validation.

last_updated_at_version_meta_to_pb maps None to absent, Inline to copied Vec bytes under InlineLastUpdatedAtVersions, and Column to an empty RowLineageColumn under ColumnLastUpdatedAtVersions. It returns Option directly, with no validation, feature flag setting or version restamping.

created_at_version_meta_to_pb mirrors the same mapping under creation-version oneof alternatives. Inline bytes are copied and column carries no file metadata. Correct carrier/feature validation belongs to separate metadata and transaction paths.

write_dataset_versions clones every run.span into pb::U64Segment, stores Some(span) and exact version, collects all protobuf runs then encode_to_vec. It returns owned protobuf bytes directly without format prefix, separate version discriminator, checksum or validation. Segment conversion is covered at rust/lance-table/src/rowids/serde.rs:257-299 and panics for standalone Ranges; a directly constructed version span with that variant reaches this panic. This source-derived case was not executed. Clone+protobuf+output buffers can coexist.

read_dataset_versions uses prost decode, mapping malformed protobuf to Internal with Failed to decode RowDatasetVersionSequence text. Every run must have span or Internal Missing positions in RowDatasetVersionRun; U64Segment::try_from errors propagate. Collects decoded runs, preserving order/versions. No cross-run positional normalization, equal-neighbor merge, empty-run filter, unique-row or length-alignment check is performed here.

rechunk_version_sequences consumes owned sequences and u64 chunk sizes plus allow_incomplete. Collects all sizes first and allocates result Vec to that count; flattens owned run vectors through Peekable. Private closures build InvalidInput diagnostics for too few (chunk index, expected size, remaining) and too many runs (processed/expected chunk counts). It returns all output sequences, not a streaming interface.

For each requested chunk create empty output and remaining size, tracking an offset into the current input run across chunks. A zero remaining input length consumes that run and retries. At true exhaustion allow_incomplete breaks, otherwise returns too-few error. Zero-size output chunks skip this loop entirely. Empty input runs are skipped only while a positive output remainder is being filled.

If input remainder exceeds chunk remainder, slice that positional portion, copy its version and retain input run with increased segment_offset. Otherwise consume run, slice its remainder, reset offset and reduce needed count. Slicing delegates U64Segment::slice with unchecked u64->usize casts. No adjacent equal-version coalescing or explicit span rebasing; actual sliced span values follow the segment implementation. Segment slicing retains numeric values through skip/take and reconstruction, silently truncates excess selection and never selects Ranges (rust/lance-table/src/rowids/segment.rs:378-387).

Every requested size produces one output sequence, including short/empty sequences under allow_incomplete and zero-size chunks. After all chunks, any peeked run causes too-many error even if it is empty; allow_incomplete does not permit excess input. Errors discard local outputs but consumed owned input/iterator progress is not recoverable from Result. No checked arithmetic or aggregate length prevalidation.

build_version_meta returns uniform inline metadata only for known positive physical_rows. It panics if row_id_meta is absent, treating presence as stable-ID sanity check without decoding it. physical_rows is authoritative even if row-ID bytes disagree. from_sequence is unwrapped although locally always Ok. Leading comment says no existing metadata, but body never checks existing creation/update metadata; caller decides whether to replace. Zero/unknown physical rows yield None.

Partial refresh documents updated local offsets and preserving untouched versions/default prev_version. Count selection prefers physical_rows, else inline row-ID decode unwrap; unlike full refresh, Column row IDs without physical_rows return NotSupported, and missing row IDs imply0. It does not consult spilled.row_ids to recover unknown count. Zero count later causes a no-op.

Existing Column last-updated metadata requires spilled[fragment.id].last_updated_at or contextual NotSupported; loaded Arc payload is deep-cloned to an owned sequence. Existing Inline decode uses load_sequence().ok(), silently replacing a decode error with prev_version defaults. A decoded/loaded sequence is lazily expanded, truncated to count and padded with prev_version; no length mismatch error. Missing metadata also defaults every row.

Partial refresh assigns current_version only for offsets<len, silently ignores out-of-range positions, and tolerates duplicates/unsorted input. It scans the full version Vec into maximal equal-version Range runs and serializes to Inline before assigning last_updated_at. No monotonic version check, creation metadata change or column-file deletion. Empty updated_offsets still recompresses/replaces metadata when row count>0. Allocation is O(rows+runs+encoded bytes); returned errors before final assignment leave fragment unchanged, though unwrap/allocation panic is possible.
